subtype: Helping a parent who is targeted [Observer]
passage:
Sunday night
I came home at four and found Papa sitting straight at the dining table, phone propped on the fruit bowl, a man in uniform on the screen. Papa put a finger to his lips. His face was grey.
On a notepad he had written: police case, do not tell family, transfer FD.
I didn't shout. I sat beside him, took his hand, and wrote under his note: Papa, this is a scam. Real police never do this. Let me.
He looked at me for a long moment, then nodded. I ended the call. His hands were shaking. He kept saying, "Forty years with a clean record, and they said I'm a criminal."
I told him he had done nothing wrong, that these people fool doctors and judges too. Then we called the cybercrime helpline together, and the bank. Nothing had gone out.
He fell asleep on the sofa by eight. I keep checking on him.
Kashish

qa.a: Papa's phone was propped on the fruit bowl.

qa.q: What was Papa feeling when he kept repeating his clean record?
qa.a: He felt shocked and ashamed, hurt that anyone could call him a criminal after forty years.

qa.q: Which of Kashish's choices helped most?
qa.a: Staying calm, writing a quiet note instead of shouting, ending the call, and calling the cybercrime helpline and the bank together without blaming Papa.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Papa to read Kashish's note?
qa.a: It likely brought relief along with some embarrassment, giving him permission to break the silence he had been ordered to keep.

grounding: An adult child finds Papa on a long fake-police call, ordered to stay silent and move money, ends it calmly and reports it without blame.

subtype: Helping a parent who is targeted [Observer]
passage:
Hafsa: Ritu, urgent. Dadi has been on a video call for 2 hrs in her room
Hafsa: some officer says her pension account is linked to a crime. she's whispering, told me to go away
Ritu: ok. stay calm. is she being asked to pay or move money?
Hafsa: she has her passbook out and is reading numbers
Ritu: go in now. gently. don't blame her. end the call yourself if you need to
Ritu: real police never keep someone on video or ask for money to clear a name
Hafsa: done. sat with her and pressed end. she's crying, says they told her she'd be arrested
Ritu: tell her she did nothing wrong. these people fool everyone. then call the cybercrime helpline and her bank now
Hafsa: calling. no money went out. she keeps saying sorry
Ritu: she has nothing to be sorry for. make her some tea. call me after

qa.q: How long had Dadi been on the video call?
qa.a: Dadi had been on the video call for 2 hrs.

qa.q: What was Dadi feeling after the call ended?
qa.a: She was frightened and ashamed, crying because they told her she would be arrested, and kept saying sorry.

qa.q: Which part of Ritu's advice mattered most in the moment?
qa.a: Telling Hafsa to go in gently, end the call and not blame Dadi, then call the cybercrime helpline and the bank, stopped the money and protected Dadi's dignity.

qa.q: What was the call like for Dadi?
qa.a: Dadi felt trapped and afraid, whispering and sending Hafsa away because the caller had convinced her she was in serious trouble.

grounding: A family member finds Dadi on a long fake-officer call reading out bank details, ends it calmly without blame, and reports it to the helpline and bank.
